source.label: Harnack's inequality in the strip as a limit of positivity certificates

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: For continuous even real g of compact support with phi(s) = Re h(s + i/2) >= 0, h the transform of g: Re h(t+iy) = (1/2pi) int phi(s) K_y(t-s) ds with K_y(t) = 2 pi cos(pi y) cosh(pi t)/(sinh^2(pi t) + cos^2(pi y)); hence Re h(gamma + iy) >= cos(pi y) cos(pi delta) exp(-pi |gamma - gamma0|) Re h(gamma0 + i delta) in the open strip; and if the sum of Re h over a multiset Z of points of the strip is at most B while c Re h(gamma0 + i delta) > B, then cos(pi delta) sum over Z of cos(pi y_rho) exp(-pi |gamma_rho - gamma0|) < c.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof (Fourier inversion, an explicit Poisson kernel of the strip, Harnack with constants), with a numerical control of the kernel and of the inequality. Limits explicit-formula certificates that require nonnegativity on the whole critical strip: they can exclude a point at distance delta from the line only where the weighted count of actual zeros near its height is below 4/cos(pi delta). The size of that count for zeta is recalled, not derived. Believed classical; no novelty claimed.
claims.rationale: Answers the second route review's decisive test: positivity on the whole strip cannot separate a point from the zeros near it, so that formulation reproduces at best the classical region where the zeros nearby are on the line.
claims.next_action: Decide what a certificate needs when positivity is required only outside a window around the height.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; one recalled integral checked numerically to 1.8e-10.
notes.significance: Context: an obstruction to a method, elementary. Novelty not claimed.
notes.relationships: The model's negative direction for the Gram form used positivity on the line only; this lemma shows the price of positivity on the strip.

relationships: That statement needs the other zeros on the line; this lemma shows what removing that hypothesis by positivity on the strip costs.
